title: The Midnight Write Freeze
subtitle: High-velocity telemetry ingestion triggers sudden storage engine write stalls

brief.narrative: During a massive citywide gang interdiction operation, 3,000 patrol cruisers, tactical vans, and aerial surveillance drones stream telemetry (GPS coordinates, biometric heart rates, dashcam telematics) at 120,000 writes/second into the department's distributed NoSQL LSM-tree cluster. Suddenly at 00:15, all write ingestion freezes. Inbound API gateways report 504 Gateway Timeouts, edge ingest buffers overflow, and real-time tactical tracking screens go pitch black. The storage engine has triggered an emergency Write Stall: incoming writes flushed Memtables to disk faster than background compaction threads could merge and compact Level 0 (L0) SSTables down to Level 1. To prevent catastrophic read amplification, the engine abruptly halted all client writes to let compaction catch up.
symptoms: Write throughput dropped from 120,000 writes/s to 0 writes/s at 00:15
API gateways accumulating thousands of 504 Gateway Timeout errors
Storage engine metric `rocksdb.num-running-compactions` saturated at max thread limit
L0 SSTable file count exceeded threshold (reached 48 files, limit: 20), triggering hard write stall
brief.objective: Diagnose why high write volume overwhelmed LSM compaction and implement a tiered compaction strategy with ingest buffering to prevent write stalls.

rootCause.question: What is the root cause of the sudden complete write freeze across the telemetry cluster?

options.text: LSM-tree compaction debt outpaced write ingestion, causing Level 0 (L0) SSTable files to accumulate past the safety threshold and trigger a hard write stall
options.feedback: Correct! In Log-Structured Merge-tree (LSM) engines, writes are appended to an in-memory Memtable and flushed to Level 0 SSTables. Leveled Compaction requires heavy disk I/O to sort and merge SSTables down to deeper levels. At 120k writes/second, disk I/O saturated, background compaction fell severely behind, and L0 files spiked to 48 (surpassing the hard limit of 20). The database activated its protective Write Stall, blocking all new writes.

options.text: The physical SSD drives ran out of raw storage space, causing the operating system filesystem to remount as read-only
options.feedback: Drive capacity telemetry shows 42TB of free disk space remaining. The issue is not raw capacity exhaustion, but compaction queue debt causing an internal software write stall.

options.text: A network switch port flapping between the API gateway and the database severed TCP connections
options.feedback: The network links are healthy with 0 dropped packets. The API gateway successfully maintains open TCP connections to the database, but those connections are frozen inside storage write-stall locks.

options.text: A distributed deadlock between row-level transactional locks on drone GPS identifiers halted thread execution
options.feedback: LSM telemetry ingestion uses blind append-only inserts without row-level read-modify-write locks or ACID transactions. Deadlocks do not apply to this workload.

fix.question: How should the storage and ingestion architecture be reconfigured to eliminate write stalls under extreme ingestion spikes?

options.text: Switch to Size-Tiered Compaction Strategy (STCS) optimized for append-only time-series data, allocate dedicated I/O rate limits for compaction threads, and buffer ingest spikes through a distributed Kafka queue
options.feedback: Correct! For time-series and append-only write-heavy workloads, Size-Tiered Compaction (or Tiered Compaction) has dramatically lower write amplification and I/O overhead than Leveled Compaction because it merges SSTables of similar sizes without immediate cross-level sorting. Adding a Kafka buffer decouples rapid fleet ingest bursts from storage disk flush limits, allowing compaction to run smoothly without stalling client gateways.

options.text: Disable background compaction entirely to eliminate disk I/O contention during operational shifts
options.feedback: Disabling compaction would cause SSTable files to accumulate indefinitely. Every read query would have to inspect thousands of separate files on disk, causing catastrophic read amplification and memory exhaustion.

options.text: Replace the LSM-tree database with a traditional B-tree relational database using synchronous foreign key constraints
options.feedback: B-tree storage engines perform random disk writes for every insert, resulting in far worse write throughput than LSM-trees and collapsing under 120,000 writes/second.

options.text: Increase the write stall threshold to 10,000 files without changing the compaction strategy or adding ingress buffering
options.feedback: Permitting 10,000 L0 files would cause read latency to explode from milliseconds to dozens of seconds, as reading any single key would require checking thousands of overlapping SSTable bloom filters.
